150:  * Input Parameters:

153:  *   buf    - Receive Buffer

162:                           uint16_t reg,
163:                           uint8_t *buf,
164:                           size_t buflen)
165: {
166:   int ret;
167: 
168:   /* Send the Register Address, MSB first */
169: 
170:   uint8_t regbuf[2] =
171:   {
172:     reg >> 8,   /* First Byte: MSB */
173:     reg & 0xff  /* Second Byte: LSB */
174:   };
175: 
176:   /* Compose the I2C Messages */
177: 
178:   struct i2c_msg_s msgv[2] =
179:   {
180:     {
181:       /* Send the I2C Register Address */
182: 
183:       .frequency = CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_I2C_FREQUENCY,
184:       .addr      = dev->addr,
185:       .flags     = 0,
186:       .buffer    = regbuf,
187:       .length    = sizeof(regbuf)
188:     },
189:     {
190:       /* Receive the I2C Register Values */
191: 
192:       .frequency = CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_I2C_FREQUENCY,
193:       .addr      = dev->addr,
194:       .flags     = I2C_M_READ,
195:       .buffer    = buf,
196:       .length    = buflen
197:     }
198:   };

200:   const int msgv_len = sizeof(msgv) / sizeof(msgv[0]);
201: 
202:   iinfo("reg=0x%x, buflen=%ld\n", reg, buflen);
203:   DEBUGASSERT(dev && dev->i2c && buf);
204: 
205:   /* Execute the I2C Transfer */
206: 
207:   ret = I2C_TRANSFER(dev->i2c, msgv, msgv_len);
208:   if (ret < 0)
209:     {
210:       ierr("I2C Read failed: %d\n", ret);
211:       return ret;
212:     }

214: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_INPUT_INFO
215:   iinfodumpbuffer("gt9xx_i2c_read", buf, buflen);

370: /****************************************************************************
371:  * Name: gt9xx_read_touch_data
372:  *
373:  * Description:
374:  *   Read a Touch Sample from Touch Panel. Returns either 0 or 1
375:  *   Touch Points.
376:  *
377:  * Input Parameters:
378:  *   dev    - Touch Panel Device
379:  *   sample - Returned Touch Sample (0 or 1 Touch Points)
380:  *
381:  * Returned Value:
382:  *   Zero (OK) on success; -EAGAIN if data is not ready; or another negated
383:  *   errno value on failure.
384:  *
385:  ****************************************************************************/
386: 
387: static int gt9xx_read_touch_data(FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *dev,
388:                                  FAR struct touch_sample_s *sample)
389: {
390:   uint8_t status[1];
391:   uint8_t status_code;
392:   uint8_t touched_points;
393:   uint8_t touch[6];
394:   uint16_t x;
395:   uint16_t y;
396:   uint8_t flags;
397:   int ret;
398: 
399:   /* Erase the Touch Sample and Touch Point */
400: 
401:   iinfo("\n");
402:   DEBUGASSERT(dev && sample);
403:   memset(sample, 0, sizeof(*sample));
404: 
405:   /* Read the Touch Panel Status */
406: 
407:   ret = gt9xx_i2c_read(dev, GTP_READ_COOR_ADDR, status, sizeof(status));
408:   if (ret < 0)
409:     {
410:       ierr("Read Touch Panel Status failed: %d\n", ret);
411:       return ret;
412:     }
413: 
414:   /* Decode the Status Code and the Touched Points */
415: 
416:   status_code = status[0] & 0x80;
417:   touched_points = status[0] & 0x0f;
418: 
419:   /* If Touch Panel Status is OK and Touched Points is 1 or more */
420: 
421:   if (status_code != 0 && touched_points >= 1)
422:     {
423:       /* Read the First Touch Point (6 bytes) */
424: 
425:       ret = gt9xx_i2c_read(dev, GTP_POINT1, touch, sizeof(touch));
426:       if (ret < 0)
427:         {
428:           ierr("Read Touch Point failed: %d\n", ret);
429:           return ret;
430:         }
431: 
432:       /* Decode the Touch Coordinates */
433: 
434:       x = touch[0] + (touch[1] << 8);
435:       y = touch[2] + (touch[3] << 8);
436: 
437:       /* Return the Touch Coordinates */
438: 
439:       flags = TOUCH_ID_VALID | TOUCH_POS_VALID;
440:       sample->npoints = 1;
441:       sample->point[0].id = 0;
442:       sample->point[0].x = x;
443:       sample->point[0].y = y;
444:       sample->point[0].flags = flags;
445:     }
446:   else if (status_code == 0)
447:     {
448:       return -EAGAIN;
449:     }
450: 
451:   /* Set the Touch Panel Status to 0 */
452: 
453:   ret = gt9xx_set_status(dev, 0);
454:   if (ret < 0)
455:     {
456:       ierr("Set Touch Panel Status failed: %d\n", ret);
457:       return ret;
458:     }
459: 
460:   return OK;
461: }

487:   const size_t outlen = sizeof(sample);

493:   iinfo("buflen=%ld\n", buflen);

541:       sample.npoints = 1;

564:  * Name: gt9xx_open
565:  *
566:  * Description:
567:  *   Open the Touch Panel Device.  If this is the first open, we power on
568:  *   the Touch Panel, probe for the Touch Panel and enable Touch Panel
569:  *   Interrupts.
570:  *
571:  * Input Parameters:
572:  *   filep - File Struct for Touch Panel
573:  *
574:  * Returned Value:
575:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.

577:  ****************************************************************************/

580: {
581:   FAR struct inode *inode;
582:   FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv;
583:   unsigned int use_count;
584:   int ret;
585: 
586:   /* Get the Touch Panel Device */
587: 
588:   iinfo("\n");
589:   inode = filep->f_inode;
590:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
591:   priv = inode->i_private;
592: 
593:   /* Begin Mutex: Lock to prevent concurrent update to Reference Count */
594: 
595:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
596:   if (ret < 0)
597:     {
598:       ierr("Lock Mutex failed: %d\n", ret);
599:       return ret;
600:     }
601: 
602:   /* Get next Reference Count */
603: 
604:   use_count = priv->cref + 1;
605:   DEBUGASSERT(use_count < UINT8_MAX && use_count > priv->cref);
606:   if (use_count == 1)
607:     {
608:       /* If first user, power on the Touch Panel */
609: 
610:       DEBUGASSERT(priv->board->set_power != NULL);
611:       ret = priv->board->set_power(priv->board, true);
612:       if (ret < 0)
613:         {
614:           goto out_lock;
615:         }
616: 
617:       /* Let Touch Panel power up before probing */
618: 
619:       nxsig_usleep(100 * 1000);
620: 
621:       /* Check that Touch Panel exists on I2C */
622: 
623:       ret = gt9xx_probe_device(priv);
624:       if (ret < 0)
625:         {
626:           /* No such device, power off the Touch Panel */
627: 
628:           priv->board->set_power(priv->board, false);
629:           goto out_lock;
630:         }
631: 
632:       priv->int_pending = false;
633:       priv->touched = false;
634: 
635:       /* Enable Touch Panel Interrupts */
636: 
637:       DEBUGASSERT(priv->board->irq_enable);
638:       priv->board->irq_enable(priv->board, true);
639:     }
640: 
641:   /* Set the Reference Count */
642: 
643:   priv->cref = use_count;
644: 
645:   /* End Mutex: Unlock to allow update to Reference Count */
646:

**Findings**

1. **High: I2C failures consume the interrupt and can corrupt the contact lifecycle**  
   [`gt9xx.c:519-526`](/home/u2fsdgvkx1/openvela/nuttx/drivers/input/gt9xx.c#L519-L526) clears `int_pending` before the transfer, but every error path exits without restoring it. This includes failures reading status/coordinates or acknowledging status at [`gt9xx.c:407-411`](/home/u2fsdgvkx1/openvela/nuttx/drivers/input/gt9xx.c#L407-L411), [`gt9xx.c:425-429`](/home/u2fsdgvkx1/openvela/nuttx/drivers/input/gt9xx.c#L425-L429), and [`gt9xx.c:453-457`](/home/u2fsdgvkx1/openvela/nuttx/drivers/input/gt9xx.c#L453-L457). Poll-driven callers can consequently sleep indefinitely despite unconsumed controller data. If a release read fails, `touched` remains true; the next physical contact will then be reported as `TOUCH_MOVE` at [`gt9xx.c:529-546`](/home/u2fsdgvkx1/openvela/nuttx/drivers/input/gt9xx.c#L529-L546), with the intervening `TOUCH_UP` and new `TOUCH_DOWN` lost. Preserve whether an interrupt was consumed and atomically restore/re-notify it for genuine I2C errors, while retaining the intended clearing behavior for `-EAGAIN`.

The normal successful state transitions and the concurrent-interrupt preservation ordering otherwise match the stated behavior. Residual risk: no tests cover I2C failures or an ISR injected during each transfer phase.
